subject: Use NA values in the covariate

messages.author: 5a65c451b9c1795b
messages.subject: Use NA values in the covariate
parts:
Hello, I am using INLA to model areal case data, taking spatial dependency into account through a neighborhood structure (MENH.adj). "OID_" identifies the areal spatial unit, of which there are 50. OID_ runs from 0 to 49. 

When I run:

formula <- caserate ~ 1 + f(OID_, model="bym",graph=MENH.adj)
model1 <- inla(formula,family="poisson",data=data)

 I am getting this error:

Error in inla(formula, family = "poisson", data = data) : 
  f(OID_). Covariate does not match 'values' 1 times. Indexes for mismatch:1. This is not what you want. Use NA values in the covariate!

OID_ runs from 0 to 49.  Is the 0 the problem?  Should it run from 1 to 50?

Thank you,

Susan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Use NA values in the covariate
parts:
hi,

yes OID_ should be integers from 1...50, as these are the nodes in the
graph MENH.adj

H
